newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila bankers reduce further OTC dlr selling rate.
newsitem.headline: Manila bankers reduce further OTC dlr selling rate.

text.p: The Bankers Association of the Philippines (BAP) said on Thursday all commercial banks had agreed to further cut their over-the-counter (OTC) dollar selling rates.
"The BAP has agreed to reduce the maximum selling spread from four percent to two percent," BAP president Deogracias Vistan told reporters after the meeting of bank presidents.
On Tuesday, the banks agreed to put a cap on their OTC selling rates equivalent to four percent above the peso's weighted average in the official foreign exchange market posted the previous day.
The weighted average on Thursday was at 28.574 to the dollar.

The decision to put a cap on the selling rate was triggered by a public outcry over moves by banks to sell dollars to customers at a rate as high as 35 pesos to the dollar when the peso was actually trading between 29 to 30 in the interbank market.
He said the spread could become narrower as normalcy returns to the foreign exchange market.
The peso fluctuated wildly, falling at one point to a 45-month low of 30 to the dollar, after the central bank on Friday allowed it to trade within a wider band.
It has since recovered, closing at 28.00 in modest trading on Thursday.
"Most banks will cut down their prime lending rate. It will still be in the 20s," Vistan added.
Some banks have lowered their rates from the 30s earlier this week.
